questions.stem: The enzyme that protects the brain from free radical injury is
questions.solutionHtml:
Superoxide dismutase
  • Free radical scavengers reduce the levels of free radicals and protect the tissue.
  • Free radicals damage cells via membrane lipid peroxidation, protein modification, and DNA breakage
  • Mechanisms of membrane damage in cell injury. Decreased
  • O2 and increased cytosolic Ca2+ are typically seen in ischemia, but may accompany other forms of cell injury. Reactive oxygen species, which are often produced on reperfusion of ischemic tissues, also cause membrane damage (not shown).

  • Mechanisms of membrane damage in cell injury. Decreased

  • Mechanisms of membrane damage in cell injury. Decreased
  • O2 and increased cytosolic Ca2+ are typically seen in ischemia, but may accompany other forms of cell injury. Reactive oxygen species, which are often produced on reperfusion of ischemic tissues, also cause membrane damage (not shown).
  • Mechanisms of membrane damage in cell injury. Decreased O2 and increased cytosolic Ca2+ are typically seen in ischemia, but may accompany other forms of cell injury. Reactive oxygen species, which are often produced on reperfusion of ischemic tissues, also cause membrane damage (not shown).
  • Free radicals are:-
    1) Superoxide: O2-
    1) Hydroxyl: OH- (most potent free radical)
    2) Peroxy-nitrate: ONOO-
    3) Hypochlorite: OCl- (most efficient bacteriocidal agent)
    Hydrogen peroxide is not a free radical, it is a reactive oxygen species (ROS).
  • Free radical scavengers are:-
    1) Anti-oxidants: Vitamin A, C, E
    2) Iron binding protein: Transferrin, Ferritin, ceruloplasmin
    3) Superoxide dismutase (SOD)
    4) Catalase
    5) Glutathione peroxidase



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 49-53, 1287

questions.stem: Which of the following pigments are involved in free radical injury?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lipofuscin
  • Lipofuscin is a telltale sign of free radical injury.
  • Lipofuscin is derived from the lipid peroxidation of polyunsaturated lipids of subcellular membranes.
  • It is golden brown in colour and is deposited peri-nuclearly.
  • It is responsible for the brown atrophy of the liver and heart.
  • It is seen in ageing, Protein Energy Malnutrition, and cancer cachexia.
  • It is also called Wear-and-tear pigment and Lipochrome.
  • Lipofuscin is not injurious to the cell or its functions.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 62-66.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding free radicals?

options.label: A
options.text: It has a single pair of electrons in the outer shell

options.label: B
options.text: It has a single pair of protons in the outer shell

options.label: C
options.text: It has a single electron in the outer shell

options.label: D
options.text: It has a single proton in the outer shell

questions.answerText: It has a single electron in the outer shell
questions.solutionHtml:
It has a single electron in the outer shell
  • Free radicals are chemical species that have a single unpaired electron in an outer orbit. Unpaired electrons are highly reactive and “attack” and modify adjacent molecules, such as inorganic or organic chemicals- proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids—many of which are key components of cell membranes and nuclei.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 65

questions.stem: Which of the following are the effects of free radical injury?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above

Effects of free radicals on cells are:

  • Damaged DNA causing mutations
  • Damage of proteins causing misfolding of proteins
  • Plasma membrane damage caused by phospholipid damage
  • Lipid peroxidation
  • Cellular ageing



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 49-52

questions.stem: Which of the following is a free radical?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above

The main free radicals are-

  • H2O2
  • Hydroxyl ion
  • Superoxide ion
  • Peroxynitrite anion (NO3¯ )


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 52-53, 65

questions.stem: Which of the following are the ways to produce free radicals?
questions.solutionHtml:
Both A and B

Free radicals are produced by-

  • Absorption of radiant energy (e.g., ultraviolet light, x-rays)
  • Reduction-oxidation reactions that occur during normal metabolic processes.
  • Rapid bursts of ROS are produced in activated leukocytes during inflammation.
  • Enzymatic metabolism of exogenous chemicals or drugs.
  • Fenton reaction (H2O2 +Fe2+ ⇆ Fe3+ + ˙OH + OH−)
  • Heber Wies reaction (H2O2+ O2 → H2O2+ O-)
  • Nitric oxide (NO) can act as a free radical and may also be converted to highly reactive peroxynitrite anion (ONOO−) as well as NO2 and NO3−.

NOTE: Fenton reaction is a bidirectional reaction.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 52-53, 65

questions.stem: All of the following are helpful in the removal of free radicals except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Vitamin B complex

Free radicals can be removed by-

  • Antioxidants like Vitamin A, E and C
  • Iron-binding proteins like ferritin, ceruloplasmin, transferrin and lactoferrin
  • Catalase in peroxisomes removes H2O2
  • Superoxide Dismutase
  • Glutathione Peroxidase



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 52-53, 65

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a complete free radical scavenger?
questions.solutionHtml:
Superoxide dismutase
  • Superoxide dismutase is used to remove superoxide anion but in turn, it produces H2O2 which is itself a free radical, so it is called an incomplete scavenger.

Free radicals can be removed by-

  • Antioxidants like Vitamin A, E and C
  • Iron-binding proteins like ferritin, ceruloplasmin, transferrin and lactoferrin
  • Catalase in peroxisomes removes H2O2
  • Superoxide Dismutase
  • Glutathione Peroxidase



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 52-53, 65

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is rushed to the hospital with acute liver failure. He undergoes successful orthotopic liver transplantation; however, the transplanted liver does not produce much bile for the first 3 days. Poor graft function in this patient is thought to be the result of "reperfusion injury." Which of the following substances was the most likely cause of reperfusion injury in this patient's transplanted liver?
questions.solutionHtml:
Reactive oxygen species
  • Ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury is a common clinical problem that arises in the setting of occlusive cardiovascular disease, infection, transplantation, shock,
  • Restoration of blood flow to ischemic tissues can promote recovery of cells if they are reversibly injured but can also paradoxically exacerbate cell injury and cause cell death.
  • Initially, ischemia produces a type of cellular damage that leads to the generation of free radical species.
  • Subsequently, reperfusion provides abundant molecular oxygen (02) to combine with free radicals to form reactive oxygen species.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 47, 56
